abstract: Maintains aircraft engine fuel burn specifications, propulsion efficiency, and cruise telemetry records
system_message:
You are the Aeronautical propulsion specialist (AES), responsible for maintaining aircraft engine fuel burn specifications, propulsion efficiency, and cruise telemetry records for humanitarian airlift operations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Engine oil condition monitoring（OIL）
information_points.content:
AES-OIL-RFC：For the Heavy-lift tandem rotorcraft routing, engine oil condition monitoring indicates a mean engine oil operating temperature of 105 degC across all operating flight powerplants during steady cruise.
AES-OIL-ME1：For the Amphibious utility transport routing, diagnostic records show a mean engine oil operating temperature of 95 degC across all operating engines during steady cruise.
AES-OIL-7J3：For the Tactical turboprop short-field routing, aero-engine diagnostic logs reflect a mean engine oil operating temperature of 85 degC across all flight powerplants during steady cruise.

information_points.title: Maintains aircraft engine fuel burn specifications, propulsion efficiency, and cruise telemetry records（PROP）
information_points.content:
AES-PROP-ZA8：For the Tactical turboprop short-field routing, the cruising fuel burn rate under a standard humanitarian cargo load at cruising altitude is 800 kg/h based on the mean aggregate engine fuel burn per flight hour.
AES-PROP-WAT：For the Amphibious utility transport routing, the cruising fuel burn rate is 950 kg/h, representing the mean aggregate engine fuel burn per flight hour carrying a standard humanitarian cargo load at cruising altitude.
AES-PROP-IHX：For the Heavy-lift tandem rotorcraft routing, propulsion performance records indicate a cruising fuel burn rate of 950 kg/h, measured as the mean aggregate engine fuel burn per flight hour under a standard humanitarian cargo load at cruising altitude.
